description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running streamed responses intermittently terminate with a dangling/partial markdown footnote and missing final paragraph when traffic flows through their corporate WAF/edge proxy. Impact: several generation responses lost trailing content (footnotes, final sentence) during the last 1-2% of token output, affecting business-critical summaries and causing downstream parsing errors in the customer's ingestion pipeline. Environment: prod (us-west) for Fintegrate enterprise account on hosted API.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer issues streaming request (SSE) for a ~1200-token summary via the standard Redwood API.
2) Traffic flows through the customer's WAF (Symantec managed appliance in front of an ALB).
3) Approximately 98-99% through the stream the client observes the final paragraph missing and a trailing footnote marker like '[1]^' with no footnote body.
4) Reconnecting the client sometimes yields duplicate prefix tokens but does not recover the lost concluding paragraph.
5) Reproduced by Support using curl with --http1.1 and by enabling websocket fallback behind an emulated WAF rule set.
logs:
Edge-proxy (us-west-2) logs show 200 chunked responses with final chunk cut and a single 0-length chunk inserted between data frames. Example tcpdump excerpt: 
- FIN/ACK midstream from WAF -> backend connection closed; upstream kept alive.
- Inserted chunk: '0

' observed before final 'data:' event, after which client parser stops.
Service logs (serving-runtime) show normal generation to end-of-stream and a final 'stream_closed_by_peer' event around the same timestamp. No 5xx recorded in runtime.
Related edge request id: rW-20260313-ff12a4
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: proxy reordering or injected zero-length chunk causes client-side parser to consider stream complete before final metadata arrives.
What we did: reproduced behind a local F5 appliance with TLS inspector rules; captured wire trace and compared server-side SSE envelope.
Findings: the backend continued to send the ending metadata block, but a 0-length chunk (likely added by the WAF's chunked response rewriter) arrived before that block and triggered some clients' SSE parsers to treat the stream as terminated. Websocket fallback path exhibited similar behavior when the proxy prematurely closed the underlying socket.
Cross-references: Slack #support (thread tXQ-298), linked internal ticket INT-4312 (edge-proxy keepalive tuning), GitHub PR to tolerate late zero-length chunk: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5423.

resolution: Workaround: Customer temporarily disabled response-body rewrite rules for /v1/streams and observed restored complete payloads. Permanent fix: engineering merged PR 5423 to make the SSE parser tolerant of an inserted zero-length chunk and to treat a socket half-close as potentially temporary (waits configurable grace window). A follow-up internal task INT-4312 remains to adjust edge-proxy keepalive behavior and add automated detection/telemetry for injected-chunk patterns. We recommended customers on enterprise WAFs to whitelist streaming endpoints or enable pass-through semantics for chunked responses.
